blogs.title: Goodbye Tokenizers? How the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) Makes AI More Efficient
blogs.description: Most large language models rely on 'tokenizers'—a rigid system that chops text into pre-defined chunks. This blog explores how the new Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) ditches this old method entirely. We'll explain how BLT processes raw bytes directly, dynamically grouping them into 'patches' only when necessary, and why this allows the model to use up to 50% less computing power during inference while matching the performance of giants like Llama 3.

blogs.title: Smarter Compute: Why Your AI Should Spend More Time on Hard Words and Less on Easy Ones
blogs.description: Traditional models waste energy treating every word equally, whether it's a complex technical term or a simple punctuation mark. This post dives into BLT's secret sauce: 'Entropy Patching.' We'll break down how the model uses a tiny helper network to predict the difficulty of the next byte, dynamically deciding where to allocate heavy computing power and where to skim through easily predictable text. Learn how this adaptive approach leads to faster speeds and smarter resource management.

blogs.title: From Typos to Low-Resource Languages: Why Raw Bytes Make AI More Robust
blogs.description: Have you noticed how some AI models get confused by typos, weird capitalization, or obscure languages? That's often because they rely on fixed token lists that don't account for individual letters. This article highlights BLT's superpower: its ability to understand text at the character level. We'll look at experimental results showing how BLT handles noisy inputs better than token-based models and excels at tasks involving spelling, phonetics, and low-resource languages where standard tokenizers fail.

blogs.title: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling: How BLT Allows You to Grow Bigger Models Without Slowing Down
blogs.description: Usually, making an AI bigger means it gets slower and more expensive to run. But BLT introduces a game-changing concept called 'Fixed-Inference Scaling.' In this post, we explain how engineers can simultaneously increase both the model size *and* the size of its data patches. The result? A significantly more powerful brain that runs just as fast as its smaller counterpart, unlocking a new frontier for efficient and capable artificial intelligence.
